title: Portable Conversation Cartridge — brainstorm
body:
Context / one-line idea:
Portable Conversation Cartridge = a compact, encrypted snapshot of a live assistant session (metadata + compressed context + policies + user preferences) that can be transferred across devices, model backends (hosted/dedicated/private), or stored as a user artifact for recall / cloning / A/B testing. Think: small reusable bundle you can pass between endpoints or to other users.

Why this matters (problems we solve):
- Continuity: users switch devices or channels and expect the assistant to pick up with minimal friction.
- Experimentation: product teams can snapshot a conversation and replay it against model variants to compare outputs without full session replay plumbing.
- Transferability: customer support or human agents can take over a conversation without leaking unnecessary state or full logs.
- Data minimization: by compressing/context pruning we can store less token history while keeping the semantic state needed for quality.

Key constraints/opportunities:
- Cartridge should be small-ish (target: <= 10KB for typical 2-4 turn state; worst-case configurable).
- End-to-end encryption (KMS integration for private deployments).
- Should be compatible across model versions and degrade gracefully if fields missing.
- Expose migration helpers that map cartridge fields to Redwood API request fields (e.g., prompt prefix, persona, sticky slots).

Rough component breakdown:
1) Cartridge schema (v0):
   - id (uuid), created_at, created_by (user id), provenance (app/route)
   - metadata: last_model_id, locale, taxonomy tags, user-visible title
   - compact_context: ordered list of (role, compressed_message) where compressed_message is tokenized + LZ4 or semantic embed + small instructions
   - policies: rate-limits, cost-sensitivity (e.g., prefer-quantized, max-tokens), fallback_rule reference
   - ui_hints: suggested system messages, persistent buttons, quick-reply templates
   - access_control: public/shared/private + recipient ids, encrypted_keys (KMS-wrapped)

2) APIs / surface:
   - POST /v1/cartridges (create) -> returns cartridge id + short URL (if allowed)
   - GET /v1/cartridges/:id (fetch) -> requires appropriate auth + unwrap KMS on fetch
   - POST /v1/consume-cartridge (model, cartridge, options) -> immediate run that maps the cartridge into a generate/chat call; returns generation + meta diff
   - PUT /v1/cartridges/:id/publish -> convert to shareable snapshot (strip sensitive tokens)

User stories (rough):
- As an end user, I switch from mobile to desktop and want the assistant to remember the last 3 exchanges and my chosen tone.
- As a support agent, I open a cartridge shared by a user and can run the same conversation against the agent persona before replying.
- As a QA engineer, I snapshot a failing convo and replay against two quantized models to see output regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- create + fetch cartridge working for hosted API with size <= 20KB for common cases
- consume-cartridge maps to a single Redwood generate/chat call and provides a deterministic mapping for system + user turns
- encryption-at-rest for cartridges in hosted (KMS) and ability to use customer KMS in Private/Dedicated
- telemetry: create/fetch/consume events appear in Console with token delta + latency

Instrumentation / metrics to watch:
- cartridge_create_rate, create_latency, fetch_latency, consume_latency
- avg_cartridge_size_bytes, p95_size
- replay_success_rate (consume that results in > 0.7 semantic similarity to original continuation - for testing)
- number of cartridges shared externally (link click-throughs)

Security & compliance notes:
- By default, cartridges should exclude raw PII by providing an opt-in flag for richer snapshots. Default: redact emails/SSNs/credit-cards.
- Provide a scrubber step during publish that runs the last N user messages through PII detector (on-host) and redact or replace with tokens.
- For Private deployments, allow customer-managed KMS wrapping; for hosted, KMS in our cloud but with explicit retention policy controls.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much do we compress vs. semantic-store? Option A: LZ4 + proto messages (cheap, reversible). Option B: embed-encode last N turns and store embeddings (non-reversible, smaller) — but harder to reconstruct exact tokens for eval.
- UX: should cartridges be first-class objects in Console? or only surfaced via app-level sharing?
- Privacy: should cartridges default to ephemeral (expire after X days) vs. persistent?
- Interoperability: how to mark fields that are "best-effort" for older model variants? fallback mapping needed.

Proto / mapping sketch (consume -> generate):
- cartridge.ui_hints.system_message -> system prompt (prepended)
- cartridge.compact_context -> last 2 system/user/assistant turns expanded (if compressed, decompress) -> appended as history
- policies.max_tokens / prefer-quantized -> map to inference params
- special: if cartridge.persistent_buttons present, include as structured tools payload (function_calls)

Experiment ideas (quick):
- A/B: replay 500 real-user cartridges against current model and a quantized variant, measure quality delta and cost savings.
- Compression ablation: 3 levels (none, LZ4, embed) compare size vs. replay fidelity.
- UX prototype: mobile -> desktop switch flow using a local file drop vs. cloud pickup; gauge friction.

Prototype checklist (next 2 sprints):
- [ ] define cartridge v0 proto (fields + wire format)
- [ ] basic create/fetch endpoints (hosted-only) + storage layer (encrypted blob)
- [ ] client-side helper: javascript SDK method to create and download a cartridge file (.rwc?)
- [ ] consume-cartridge mapping in runtime (small adapter)
- [ ] write 3 small integration tests (create -> consume -> compare)

Notes / UX sketches (brain dump):
- UX copy: "Save this conversation as a cartridge" -> choose visibility: "Just me / Link / Team" -> optional expiry -> (advanced) redact PII
- Idea: cartridges as "playlists" of prompt presets + last context (for creators to publish prompt packs)
- Mobile quick share: offer "Export cartridge" -> share via QR or link; other device scans link, fetches cartridge after auth

Slack references & back-links:
- convo-portables discussion: #product-conversations (thread tbd)
- related PRD: convo-resume (see linked Linear ticket)

Stuff to surface to eng-design review:
- storage cost model: avg cartridge size * retention days * user base -> ballpark estimate
- backwards compatibility guarantees for cartridge schema

Draft timeline (very rough):
- Week 1-2: schema + API sketch + internal prototype (hosted only)
- Week 3: SDK helpers + mobile quick-share demo
- Week 4: replay experiments + QA + internal docs

If we want to move this forward: immediate asks for owners:
- @Maya: help scope PII scrubber and UX copy
- @Noah: feasibility for runtime mapping + cost model (cartridge loads per second)
- @Asha: KMS/customer-key integration constraints (private deployments)

Random reminders to self:
- Keep the wire format stable (v0 -> v1 migration plan)
- Think about archival vs. ephemeral costs separately in Console pricing
- Consider a tiny CLI tool for offline QA engineers to batch replay cartridges

End of scratchpad — lots to refine but feels like a concrete, useful primitive for continuity and experimentation.
